experiment.try: Read RemoteMCP.ask and ran RemoteMCP.test.mjs: checked the async ask (54d1fb3b1, live since 18:33) against the owner's worry that an interrupted ask loses its answer.
experiment.result: Timeout and wait:false: covered. RemoteMCP.test.mjs passes (ok 7 calls), and a late answer lands in voice-app's inbox for updates. Cancel: not covered and not proven. RemoteMCP only notices a cancel when res or its socket is destroyed. An MCP client cancels with notifications/cancelled, which post() answers 202 and ignores (line 99). Through the Cloudflare tunnel, the origin socket may stay open. If the cancel goes unnoticed and the answer arrives inside the minute, deliver(false) marks it sent and returns it into a dead response, so it is lost. That is the owner's suspicion, and the code allows it. Two more gaps: watchers are in memory, so an answer written across a Servex restart is never delivered; and Servex cannot know the model read a returned answer. Today's five asks took 17-45 s; none timed out.
experiment.measure: Does an interrupted or late ask still reach updates?
experiment.next: Fix (vscode-mastermind's door): (1) always put every answer in voice-app's inbox, even when it is returned, with reply_to = the question id, so the agent skips duplicates; then it always arrives. (2) Handle notifications/cancelled by requestId. (3) At boot, deliver any remote-replies file not yet marked delivered. Add a cancel case to the test.
